executiveSummary: GM1931 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract, and its 2025 administrative base is coherent: 57,798 residents, 68 neighbourhoods in twelve districts, eleven BAG places, 38 BRT settlement labels, 138 scheduled-transit stop areas, no conventional rail station and six NWB logical road links. Neighbourhood rows differ by only 28 residents (-0.048%) from the municipality control and are correctly reconciled without rewriting CBS observations. Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Krimpenerwaard is a low, subsiding peat-polder system enclosed by the Lek, Hollandsche IJssel and Vlist. Its own climate strategy says a primary Lek/IJssel breach can produce two to four metres of water and disable electricity, internet and telephony; HHSK is strengthening 10.5 km of non-compliant Hollandsche IJssel defence through 2031. Yet the generic river preset emits exactly 1.767869 m from T+12 through T+72, 30,167 affected people-equivalent and 2,017,337.569 deprived person-hours at T+72 without selecting a river level, defence segment/state, breach, connected LIWO footprint, arrival or recession. Nine active T+24 presets reuse one neighbourhood order led by rural Het Beijersche and Bonrepas, including heat, cyber and wildfire. Pluvial water is forced to exact zero at T+48 despite official warning that subsidence constantly changes low roads and that sewer, surface water and overland flow interact. The graph also presents the Schoonhoven-Gelkenes N216 ferry as a 150-unit regional road, while high-water closure of Veerpoort/landing structures and the N210-Algerabrug dependency are outside the scenario. Public water-control, sewer, water-level, transport, care, electricity, drinking-water, communications and preparedness sources substantially improve context but do not establish live state, topology, capacity or restoration. Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static-register presence must never appear as zero, open or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1931 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS feature retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1931 as Krimpenerwaard in Zuid-Holland and reports 57,798 residents, 24,561 households, density 390/km² and a rounded 23% aged 65 or older; the app retains 22.6% age 65+ and 7,874 one-person households.

Sixty-eight neighbourhood rows in twelve districts sum to 57,770 residents, 28 below the municipality control (-0.048%); households sum to 24,530 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 13,055. Allocation reconciles to 57,798 without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies Ammerstol, Bergambacht, Berkenwoude, Gouderak, Haastrecht, Krimpen aan de Lek, Lekkerkerk, Ouderkerk aan den IJssel, Schoonhoven, Stolwijk and Vlist. BRT supplies 38 labels: twenty buurtschappen, one deelkern, four gehuchten and thirteen woonkernen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0.

The generalized app MultiPolygon has 141 coordinate positions, while the fresh non-generalized CBS municipality feature has 2,586. Home/housing fields cover about 63/68 rows, cars per household 49/68, benefits 65/68 and doctor/supermarket distance 68/68; district heat and charging cover 0/68. Null and suppression remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Klimaatadaptatiestrategie and Programma Riolering en Klimaatadaptatie 2023–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Climate strategy adopted December 2021; PR&K 2023–2027; current municipal page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The late-2019 stress test is explicitly a theoretical moment snapshot: subsidence leaves low roads/locations vulnerable, but some mapped streets have since been raised and other streets will become vulnerable. The municipality says sewer, surface water and overland flow interact and sensitive areas require deeper integrated study.

The strategy requires main emergency approach routes to remain available and interprets that operationally as at most 30 cm of water on the road. Its planning framework keeps main roads passable up to 20 cm and protects vital/ vulnerable objects for water depths up to 200 cm. These are policy/design criteria, not observed passability.

For a primary Lek or IJssel breach the strategy states a broad two-to-four-metre municipal consequence and expects electricity, internet and telephony failure; it separately identifies regional Vlist failure. This is official planning context, not one selected hydraulic event or a uniform local depth.

The PR&K reports roughly 2,500 municipal pumps/pressure-sewer pumps, daily telemetry review, a goal to fix pump failures within 24 hours, dry-weather storage of 24 hours for qualifying foul/mixed systems, 54% mixed free-flow sewer, 25 km drainage and 205 km mechanical sewer. It also notes vulnerable pump power cables, incomplete pressure-main risk detail and phased system modelling/monitoring. Design goals and asset totals do not prove live state, capacity or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard / Hoogwaterbeschermingsprogramma
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Krimpenerwaard water system, KIJK primary-defence works, dike openings and drought/freshwater operations
evidenceSources.edition: HWBP page updated March 2026; KIJK realisation 2025–2031; HHSK current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: KIJK covers 10.5 km of primary Hollandsche IJssel defence between Krimpen aan den IJssel, Ouderkerk and Gouderak where height and stability do not meet the current legal norm. The narrow dike is the only through road, has about 800 homes/businesses along it and construction includes cables and pipes; realisation runs from 2025 to 2031.

HHSK says the Krimpenerwaard is a roughly 130 km² water-rich peat-meadow system with vlieten, weteringen and many parcel ditches; subsidence affects level control, and waterlogging, scarcity and sea-level rise require system and defence adaptation. Static policy/project status does not establish current strength or failure probability.

Dike openings at Krimpen aan de Lek and Schoonhoven serve ferry/road access and must close at high water: the Krimpen ferry opening at NAP +3.50 m and Veerpoort Schoonhoven at NAP +2.70 m. Annual closure tests can delay traffic; thresholds do not prove present closure or ferry availability.

During the 2026 dry period HHSK routed fresh Lek water through Krimpenerwaard toward the Hollandsche IJssel to oppose salinity and maintain levels, and inspected drought-sensitive dikes/kades. The 1 September page says most temporary measures had ended after rain. These are timestamped operational reports and system-direction evidence, not the state of a timeless synthetic scenario.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — GM1931 risk page, Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2026 and regional crisis plan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023–2026; regional crisis plan December 2024 for 2024–2027
supports: VRHM describes Krimpenerwaard as eleven cores and dispersed hamlets between Gouda and Rotterdam, surrounded by Hollandsche IJssel, Lek and Vlist and crossed by N207, N210 and N228; it assigns relatively high local relevance to flooding/waterlogging and road/water/air incidents.

The official primary-defence scenario says inundation can also come from Lek or IJssel, impact depends on breach number/location, water height/duration, defence and road state, access may fail, people may need to self-support for days, and infrastructure recovery may not start for weeks to months.

For regional-kering failure, a polder may fill within hours; emergency pumping can take two to five days before cleanup and repair begins. VRHM explicitly identifies Krimpenerwaard as extra vulnerable because drought worsens subsidence, and distinguishes horizontal evacuation from vertical shelter while warning of damaged roads and congestion.

The crisis plan defines notification, scaling, leadership, information, resources, communications and aftermath as core processes, with hazard/object detail in separate plans. Public profile/plan pages do not provide a machine incident feed, live resources, shelter decisions or a standard reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO candidate inventory and timestamped water, weather and air observations/forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; deployment observations/forecasts retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: Exact containment against the full 2025 boundary finds nine LIWO primary catalogue points: six Hollandsche IJssel, Lek Schoonhoven, Lekkerkerk and one labelled Nieuwe Maas/Krimpen aan den IJssel; it also finds two Stein regional candidates and one regional-water-system Dijkring15 candidate. No outside-dike or supraregional-stress point is contained. Markers and probability-band flags support scenario selection, not an active breach, selected footprint or probability estimate; empty categories do not mean safe.

Waterinfo assigns two observations: Krimpen aan de Lek/Lek 92 cm NAP and Schoonhoven 42 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026, plus T+1/6/12/24/48 forecast point snapshots valid on 3–5 September. It supplies no selected T+72 series, defence state or inland depth. Point levels cannot validate the canonical 1.767869 m flood.

No KNMI station or RIVM PM2.5 monitor is assigned inside GM1931. Cabauw is the nearest KNMI station at 13.84 km and observed 17.6°C, 6.27 m/s gust and zero hourly rain at 23:30Z on 2 September; Ridderkerk-Hogeweg is the nearest PM2.5 point at 13.72 km and observed 3.9 µg/m³ at 17:00Z. Missing local points are Unknown, not zero weather or pollution.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute and public/non-mission-critical; KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0 and RIVM air observations are hourly indicative context. LIWO is versioned/irregular professional information whose layer-specific units, resolution, coverage, licence and NoData must be retained.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Zuid-Holland / OVapi / ferry operators
evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB gateways, N210/Algerabrug and scheduled bus/ferry context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; current road/ferry pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph supplies six mobility/supply-only records: N207 to Gouda, N210 toward Krimpen aan den IJssel and Lopik, N216 toward Molenlanden and N228 toward Gouda and Oudewater. The paired N210 and paired N228 sides are one physical corridor each and their nominal 150 scenario units are non-additive, not measured capacity.

The N216 edge crosses the Lek from Schoonhoven toward Gelkenes/Molenlanden via a vehicle ferry, and its NWB road-part class is VDA, but the simulator labels it a regional road with 150 units. The operator says the ferry carries traffic up to heavy freight and normally uses two vessels at weekday peaks; published schedule/capability is not incident throughput or availability.

The N210 corridor reaches Rotterdam through Krimpen aan den IJssel and the Algerabrug. The bridge was closed to road traffic 10 August–7 September 2026 for major maintenance, with potential detours over an hour; HHSK/municipality monitored N210/N207 and emergency response times. That dated closure proves corridor sensitivity, not scenario-time closure.

No conventional ProRail station lies inside GM1931. OVapi GTFS version 9543, retrieved 31 August under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, yields 138 stop areas including Bergstoepseveer, Gouderak Veerstoep, Hekendorp Veer and Schoonhoven Veer. Schedules and stop names do not establish passengers, vehicles, ferry operation, emergency use or accessibility.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, electricity planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Generalized-boundary assignment finds 378 HWH records: 188 weirs, 141 sewer pumps, forty surface-water pumps, six wastewater-treatment works and three sluices. HWH Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0. Presence does not establish complete topology, compatible units, telemetry, live state, power/backup or restoration.

One NBNL postcode sample, 2825BG, maps to Stedin Waaiersluis. Existing/required withdrawal and injection are null, while both queues and request counts are scoped zero; fourteen projects have earliest year 2026. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning is not municipality coverage, load, outage, switching or emergency reserve; exact licence identifier was not found. Null must not be coerced to zero, and queue zero is not resilience.

RDI assigns 106 antenna installations: 38 mobile, 37 fixed-link, 27 amateur, two broadcast and two other-mobile; its WFS states no reuse licence or cadence. Daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns 37 education locations: 25 primary, six secondary and six other registered. Points do not establish radio coverage, occupancy, shelter role, backup or operation.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns no emergency department inside GM1931. Groene Hart Ziekenhuis in Gouda is nearest at 7.52 km straight-line and reports 24/7 emergency/acute obstetric care, twenty rooms and 26,185 visits in 2025. Questionnaire values are not route travel time, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or guaranteed capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Oasen / Stedin / Rijkswaterstaat Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Drinking-water source, electricity works and external-safety registry context
evidenceSources.edition: Oasen annual report 2025; current Stedin and monthly REV services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Oasen's 2025 report identifies a Bergambacht wellfield that abstracts Lek bank-filtrate for treatment at Rodenhuis and regional supply around Gouda; fifteen wells are being replaced through 2027. Annual source/project context does not establish Krimpenerwaard pressure zones, current water quality, storage, outage or restoration.

Stedin reports that Berkenwoude voltage quality is below the desired level and is adding a medium-voltage connection from Kortenoord/Nieuwerkerk and a distribution station. The broader Langeland congestion study includes part of Krimpenerwaard and planned expansion. Planning congestion is not a blackout, local feeder topology, spare emergency capacity or repair promise.

The monthly CC0 REV INSPIRE Seveso point and polygon bbox query returns no feature for the inspected Krimpenerwaard extent. That scoped no-match means no record in those specific harmonized Seveso collections, not absence of fuels, farm chemicals, vessels, pipelines, dangerous-goods movements or contaminated floodwater.

No public source establishes live electricity, gas, drinking-water or industrial state. Safe use requires provider/source, edition, issue/valid time, coverage, security review, topology class, units, confidence and NoData; static project/register facts remain context-only.

evidenceSources.title: E09 — First-72-hour public preparedness and emergency-support-point status
evidenceSources.edition: Current public guidance and August 2026 municipal pilot report inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Regional guidance tells households to prepare for 72 hours with nine litres of water per person, shelf-stable food, battery radio tuned to Radio West 89.3 FM, power bank, light, first aid and warmth. This is preparedness advice, not measured household readiness or a supply entitlement.

Municipal crisis guidance uses siren, NL-Alert, regional broadcasting and hollandsmiddenveilig.nl; on evacuation it tells residents to follow police routes and go to an opvangcentrum or people outside the area, and states institutions arrange special transport for dependent people, older residents and pupils. It publishes no event-valid destination, capacity, vehicle or route plan.

An August 2026 municipal report says VRHM and municipalities are piloting emergency support points for prolonged electricity/communications loss, envisioned at recognizable places with communications and generators. It does not publish selected GM1931 locations, capacities, activation, endurance or staffing.

The model has no accountable warning, evacuation/vertical-shelter, vulnerable transport, ferry/dike closure, support-point activation, emergency pumping, care-transfer, resource, verification or re-entry action ledger.

Lek, Hollandsche IJssel, Vlist, primary/regional defences, kade openings, compartments, polder/boezem levels, terrain, ditches, assets, buildings and roads cannot be inferred from the municipal centre or overview polygon.

No place-centre mismatch was found.

Waterinfo, KNMI, air and road/project reports retain observation/valid time and limited coverage and cannot be aligned silently to canonical T+0.

Defence, kade opening, pump, water-quality, ferry/road, care, utilities, communications, industrial, resource and restoration states remain Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical scenarios execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1931 pnpm audit:model passed two tests covering ten presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/facilities/supply.
Focused inline Vite SSR reproduction captured each preset at T+24/T+72 plus full river, coastal, pluvial and compound trajectories without a repository scratch test.
Earthquake is direct-zero by T+24; wildfire has smoke/drought but zero local flame; coastal has zero direct water but indirect wind/service stress; cyber has no selected target.
Outputs are deterministic exercise indices and resident-equivalents, not observations, probabilities, casualties, measured depths, route states or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal ledgers and cumulative burden pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; hazards, demand, delivery, affected residents and deprived person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero intensity returns exact zero event hazard, affected population and attributable burden; repeated runs are deterministic and burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 68 neighbourhoods and reconciles to 57,798 residents; local demand/delivery closes and layer selection does not mutate the scenario.
Passing arithmetic does not validate water depth, spatial allocation, ferry/route feasibility, transient occupancy, dependency topology or restoration precision.

spatialPlausibility.summary: An unselected river scalar and shared neighbourhood seed conflict with the defence/polder system and local climate evidence.
notes: River depth rises from zero at T+0 to 0.622290 m at T+6 and 1.767869 m at T+12, then remains exact through T+72 without a selected level, defence/breach, compartment, footprint, arrival or recession.

Storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound at T+24 all rank Het Beijersche, Bonrepas, Prinsessenbuurt, Boven-Haastrecht and Ouderkerk aan den IJssel first in that order.

Het Beijersche and Bonrepas have only 370 and 140 residents and densities 65 and 51/km² respectively, yet lead heat and cyber. The stress test instead emphasizes changing low roads, connected sewer/surface flow, limited core heat and hotter industry sites.
A common seed cannot substitute for defence/terrain/hydraulic cells, sewer/catchment, heat/shade, eligible peat/vegetation fuel, plume/source/target, buildings, activity or exposed-object geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Logical roads stay separate from utilities, but water control, ferry/access, care, communications and utility dependencies remain absent or synthetic.
notes: Six NWB links support mobility/supply only, avoiding false road-derived utility topology, but lack selected flood/closure intersections, physical mode for N216, direction, passability, measured capacity and destinations.
The 378 HWH records and municipal 2,500-pump statement do not form an approved surface-water–polder–sewer–pump–AWZI graph and do not affect drainage/water recovery.
One NBNL sample, Stedin/Oasen project facts, 106 antennas, 37 schools and external acute care provide no physical continuity, occupancy, priority, backup or incident-state edges.
Exact service percentages remain transparent synthetic indices pending safe aggregate authority/operator/facility calibration.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but event selection, evidence time and accountable first-72-hour actions remain outside the graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.
Public layers correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; trace does not select LIWO footprint, defence/kade/pump/ferry state, Waterinfo event, route, facility, occupancy or utility topology.

A foreseeable flood needs a pre-impact warning phase plus evacuation versus vertical shelter, dike-opening/route closure, rescue, care transfer, emergency pumping/dewatering, support-point activation and re-entry decisions.
Actions lack accountable owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound disruption is directionally conservative, but exact plateaus and rapid pluvial drying are not locally calibrated.
notes: River T+72 retains exactly 1.767869 m, severity 0.554509, pressure 0.510470, 30,167 affected and 2,017,337.569 person-hours; availability ranges from drainage 0.219652 to supply 0.691715 and is unchanged after T+24 except facilities declining by T+48.

Compound T+72 retains exactly 0.373611 m, pressure 0.540854, 32,642 affected and 2,108,388.044 person-hours; power/water/drainage/gas/telecom/mobility/supply plateau after T+24 while facilities declines.

Pluvial direct depth/affected becomes exact zero at T+48 and operational by T+72, although the official stress test says changing subsided low roads and linked sewer/surface/overland systems require location-specific study. Regional-kering dewatering alone may take two to five days.

Keep conservative repair blocking as a synthetic exercise guard, expose uncertainty and do not imply local recovery promises until compartments, drainage topology, access and authority milestones are selected.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, places and demographic controls reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM1931, Krimpenerwaard, Zuid-Holland and Hollands-Midden agree; the centre and all place/neighbourhood records are coherent. CBS reports 57,798 residents and neighbourhood rows differ by -28 (-0.048%).
findings.action: Retain source editions, licence, suppression/null semantics and published-versus-allocated reconciliation without rewriting rounded observations.

findings.summary: Sparse fields and scoped empty queries remain Unknown rather than false zero or safe state.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging, provider topology/state, local acute-care/weather/air points, existing/required NBNL capacity and selected LIWO footprints are absent or null. REV Seveso and LIWO outside-dike/supraregional candidate queries return no match only within their stated coverage.
findings.action: Keep source coverage, retrieval/effective time, edition, licence, quality, suppression and NoData through ingestion, aggregation, simulation eligibility and UI; distinguish a scoped observed zero from Unknown.

findings.summary: A generic scalar emits an unsupported exact 1.767869 m Lek/IJssel flood through T+72.
findings.evidence: Depth reaches 0.622290 m at T+6 and 1.767869 m at T+12, then stays exact through T+72 with 30,167 affected and 2,017,337.569 person-hours. The municipality says a primary Lek/IJssel breach can cause two to four metres, but no river level, defence/state, breach, connected grid, arrival, velocity, probability or recession is selected; LIWO points are catalogue candidates only.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing depth, exposure and recovery until HHSK/RWS/VRHM select a versioned event. Retain the scalar only as a non-operational diagnostic and preserve non-selected cells as Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: Horizontal evacuation versus local vertical shelter is absent despite deep-water and access-loss evidence.
findings.evidence: The official local range is two to four metres for a primary breach, and VRHM warns regional water may fill polders within hours, roads may fail and mass movement can congest. The river scenario crosses 0.6 m by T+6 but starts without warning, accountable decision, zone, population movement, safe vertical location, dependent-person assistance, route/destination or verification.
findings.action: Add pre-impact owner/trigger/action ledgers for warning, evacuation versus vertical shelter, vulnerable transport, route/ferry/dike closure, rescue, care transfer, support points and re-entry; keep timing, capacity and execution Unknown until authorised/event-valid.

findings.summary: Nine unrelated active hazards reuse one neighbourhood ordering led by two sparse rural areas.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound all rank Het Beijersche, Bonrepas, Prinsessenbuurt, Boven-Haastrecht and Ouderkerk first. Het Beijersche and Bonrepas have densities 65 and 51/km², while local evidence requires distinct terrain/defence, sewer, heat/industry, fuel, plume and target mechanisms.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and source/target/exposed-object intersections. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking only after evidence-derived values and keep unsupported cells Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: Changing subsidence, groundwater, sewer and surface-water mechanisms are absent from pluvial/drought allocation and recovery.
findings.evidence: The 2019 stress maps are explicitly a changing moment snapshot; some roads have since been raised and other low points emerge. The PR&K requires linked sewer–surface–overland SSW modelling and phased monitoring. The model emits exact 0.361782 m at T+12/24, zero at T+48 and operational T+72 without a selected hyetograph, terrain/raising edition, sewer/surface state or groundwater condition.
findings.action: Obtain governing stress-test/SSW/groundwater datasets with terrain and intervention editions, rainfall assumptions, units, cells, uncertainty and NoData; do not reuse 2019 maps or point readings as live state.

findings.summary: Polder, sewer, pump, AWZI, freshwater and drinking-water dependencies are visible but not causal.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 378 points while the municipality reports roughly 2,500 pumps/pressure-sewer pumps, 24-hour dry-weather storage goals, daily telemetry, vulnerable power cables and incomplete pressure-main studies. HHSK routes Lek freshwater across the area and Oasen operates a Bergambacht Lek bank-filtrate wellfield. No approved topology, compatible capacity, live state, backup, water quality or restoration affects water/drainage.
findings.action: Build an HHSK/municipality/Oasen-approved non-sensitive compartment–surface–sewer–pump–AWZI/source graph with event-valid states and backup bands; keep registry points, design targets and missing connections non-causal and Unknown.

findings.summary: The N216 ferry is misclassified as a 150-unit road and critical dike/Algerabrug dependencies are omitted.
findings.evidence: The Schoonhoven–Gelkenes N216 crossing is a vehicle ferry (NWB class VDA) but the graph labels it regional with nominal 150. HHSK closes Veerpoort at NAP +2.70 m and the Krimpen ferry opening at +3.50 m; KIJK's dike is the only through road, while N210 depends on Algerabrug. findings.action: Correct N216 to a typed ferry with non-additive physical identity and Unknown capacity/status; add selected-event intersections for ferry landings, dike roads, N207/N210/N228 and Algerabrug with direction, decision time and care/shelter destinations.

findings.summary: Cross-boundary acute care, vulnerable transport, schools, antennas and support points cannot influence first-72-hour priorities.

The municipality has 37 education records and 106 antennas, and an emergency-support-point pilot but no published local sites. None supplies occupancy, referral/access, facility role, coverage, power/backup, activation or endurance.

findings.summary: Coastal, wildfire/smoke, industrial, earthquake and cyber outputs are narrow synthetic exercises rather than all-clear states.

findings.summary: Exact T+24–72 flood/service plateaus and rapid pluvial clearing have no local milestone contract.
findings.evidence: River depth stays 1.767869 m after T+12 and most services plateau after T+24; compound stays 0.373611 m through T+72. Conversely pluvial depth becomes zero at T+48. VRHM says regional dewatering can take two to five days and primary-flood infrastructure recovery may not start for weeks to months, depending on access, water and damage.
findings.action: Replace exact plateau/clear transitions with evidence-classed uncertainty envelopes and owner-verified milestones for water exclusion, pumping, route access, inspection, utility isolation/repair, care/facility readiness and re-entry.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route/ferry guarantee or operator commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality total; null statistics, provider, capacity, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.

The 141-position overview is suitable for display/selection, not defence, hydraulic, rainfall, sewer, groundwater, terrain, asset, building or route intersection; use the full 2,586-position geometry.
The municipal climate strategy's two-to-four-metre range and 2019 stress maps are planning/scenario evidence, not a uniform depth, current probability, live inundation, current terrain or road state.

Nine primary, two regional and one regional-water-system LIWO points are catalogue candidates, not active breaches or selected footprints; empty outside-dike/supraregional candidate queries do not prove safety.
Waterinfo Lek/Schoonhoven observations and forecasts are timestamped points without selected defence/footprint or complete T+72 series and cannot be silently aligned to synthetic T+0.
No KNMI weather or RIVM PM2.5 station is assigned inside GM1931; nearest external values are timestamped point context and no-match is not zero weather, smoke or pollution.
KIJK, dike-opening thresholds and drought/freshwater reports identify mechanisms and dated work/operations, not current strength, closure, flow, failure or restoration.

HWH's 378 assigned records and the municipal roughly 2,500 pumps are differently scoped inventories/planning statements; neither establishes completeness, connectivity, live state, capacity, power, backup or restoration.
NWB/NDW, GTFS, ferry pages, provider/project pages, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records do not establish live passability, operation, occupancy, physical topology, capacity, backup or repair.
N216 is physically a ferry but currently modelled as a regional road; its 150 scenario units must not be interpreted as throughput or continuity.
Registered residents do not equal people at farms, industrial sites, schools, ferries, recreation, events, care sites or evacuation/support locations; incident-time occupancy is not consumed.
The monthly harmonized REV Seveso no-match is limited to those collections and does not mean no hazardous materials, dangerous-goods transport, contaminated floodwater or industrial incident.

No complete public electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, stock, staffing, crew or restoration topology is consumed; unavailable/security-sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Direct coastal/fire/earthquake zero is a narrow model statement, not no storm-surge/defence, smoke/peat-fire, seismic, access, supply or cascading effect.

Recovery after T+72, pre-impact lead time, cross-boundary defence/service consequences, shelter/care destinations and capacity, mutual aid and resource constraints remain outside locally validated scope.
